quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (f. nom. sg.: quae sententia) · also interrog. adj., n. nom. pl. (quae sint ea nūmina) · also exclam. adj., n. acc. pl. (quae bella exhausta canebat!; quae … regna) · also interrog. pron./adj., n. acc. pl., what? (quae quibus anteferam; quae … maiora) · also f. nom. pl. (quae … acies)
quam: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. acc. sg.); quam (adv.), how; than · prius… quam (conj.), before, until · indef. after sī/nē, any, some (f. acc. sg.: si quam) · also interrog. adj., what? which? (f. acc. sg.: quam arcem?) · also tam … quam, as … as (adv./conj.) · also quam multa … sic, as many as … so · also ante … quam, before (conj., antequam split: non ante … quam)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.) · interrog. adj./pron., who? which? (m. nom. sg./pl.: Sed vos qui tandem) · also exclam. adj., what (youths)! (m. nom. pl.: Quī iuvenēs!)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.) · also adverbially, why? (n. acc. sg.) · also indef. after sī, anything (n. nom./acc. sg.: sī quid) · also indef. after nē, anything (nē quid inexpertum)
quis: quī, quae, quod — who (rel., dat./abl. pl., old form = quibus); also quis, who? (interrog.) · also indefinite quis, anyone (after nē/neu, m. nom. sg.); quis locus, which place? (interrog. adj.) · also indef. after sī, anyone (m. nom. sg.: sī quis) · also indef. after quam (m. nom. sg.: quam quis, until anyone) · also indef. after rel. quae (m. nom. sg.: quae quis, whatever any man)
quisve: quis, quid — who, what, anyone (interrog./indef., m. nom. sg.) + -ve, or
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quoniam: quoniam (conj.) — since, seeing that, because, whereas
rebus: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (abl./dat. pl.)
refellam: refellō, -ere, refellī — to refute, disprove, rebut (1st sg. fut.)
regebat: regō, -ere, rēxī, rēctum — to rule, govern (3rd sg. imperf.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
ruina: ruīna, -ae (f.) — collapse, downfall, ruin (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)
rumpi: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst, sever (pres. pass. inf.)
saeva: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, savage, cruel (n. acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (Gorgone saevā); n. nom./acc. pl. · also f. nom. sg. (dea saeva)
salutem: salūs, salūtis (f.) — safety, welfare, deliverance (acc. sg.)
sancta: sānctus, -a, -um — holy, sacred (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
scilicet: scīlicet (adv.) — of course, doubtless, forsooth (often ironical)
scissa: scindō, -ere, scidī, scissum — to tear, rend (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.) · also f. nom. sg.
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
segnior: sēgnis, -e — slow, sluggish; sēgnior (compar.), more sluggish (m./f. nom. sg.)
sequamur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (1st pl. pres. subj., hortatory: let us follow; deponent)
sequitur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, come after (3rd sg. pres. of deponent)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
solo: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, floor, soil (abl./dat. sg.) · also sōlus, -a, -um, alone (m./n. abl. sg.: in solo Volcente)
sonant: sonō, -āre, -uī, -itum — to sound, resound, rattle, speak (3rd pl. pres.)
soror: soror, sorōris (f.) — sister (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (Anna soror)
spicula: spīculum, -ī (n.) — sharp point, dart, arrowhead (acc. pl.)
stans: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand; stāns (pres. part., m./f./n. nom. sg.)
stat: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand; be fixed (3rd sg. pres.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subita: subitus, -a, -um — sudden, unexpected (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (subita … vox)
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
subitum: subitus, -a, -um — sudden, unexpected (n. nom. sg., with monstrum; m. acc. sg.)
successu: successus, -ūs (m.) — success, good fortune; advance (abl. sg.)
summa: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (rēs summa; summa diēs)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
superat: superō, -āre — to overcome, surpass, overpower (3rd sg. pres.)
superis: superus, -a, -um — upper, above; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tanti: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. pl.; n. gen. sg.) · also m. gen. sg. (tantī … luctūs)
tanto: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m./n. abl. sg.)
tantos: tantus, -a, -um — so great, so much (m. acc. pl.)
tantus: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. sg.)
telis: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (abl./dat. pl.)
tendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend, direct one's way (3rd sg. pres.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
testaturque: testor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to call to witness, attest (3rd sg. pres., deponent) + -que, and
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
torquent: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl (3rd pl. pres.)
trahunt: trahō, -ere, trāxī, tractum — to draw, drag, lead on (3rd pl. pres.)
trepidae: trepidus, -a, -um — alarmed, anxious, trembling (f. nom. pl.; also gen./dat. sg.)
trepidos: trepidus, -a, -um — alarmed, anxious, agitated, hurried (m. acc. pl.)
trucidant: trucīdō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to slaughter, cut down (3rd pl. pres.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbata: turbō, -āre — to disturb, throw into confusion (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
turne: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (voc. sg.)
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
ufens: Ūfēns, -entis (m.) — Ufens, Aequian leader; also a river of Latium (voc. sg.; nom. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
urbis: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (gen. sg.) · also = urbēs, nom./acc. pl. (old -īs spelling)
usque: usque (adv.) — all the way, continuously, ever, without ceasing
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent) · also + subj., oh that (wish: ut … ludar)
vacuas: vacuus, -a, -um — empty, void, unoccupied (f. acc. pl.)
velit: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
venientem: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come, approach (pres. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
victi: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer; victī, the conquered (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
victoria: victōria, -ae (f.) — victory (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
victum: victus, -ūs (m.) — living, food, sustenance (acc. sg.) · also vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg., victum volnere)
victus: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, overcome (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
videbit: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. fut.)
videres: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. impf. subj.)
vidi: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. perf.)
vocantem: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, call upon (pres. part., m. acc. sg.)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
voluit: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want (3rd sg. perf.) · also a misprint for volvit, from volvō, turns over (3rd sg. pres.)
voluntas: voluntās, -ātis (f.) — will, wish, purpose, resolve (nom. sg.)
volvitur: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, tumble (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
